courses.title: Reference planes: create, select and sketch
courses.objective: Create planes from the right-click face menu, select them by outline or label, drag the offset, sketch on a plane and use planes for extrude-up-to, mirror, split and pattern.

steps.title: A block to work on
steps.learn: Start with a 120 × 80 × 30 mm block.
instructions: Sketch a centred 120 × 80 rectangle on XY.
Extrude it 30 mm.
steps.why: Planes are easiest to learn on simple faces you can see clearly.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Right-click a face → New plane here › On face
steps.learn: The fastest way to make a plane is from the face you are looking at.
instructions: Right-click the top face of the block.
Hover New plane here ▸ and choose On face.
The plane appears in blue, selected, with its toolbar on top of the view.
steps.why: A plane on a face keeps following that face when you edit the block — it is parametric.

checkpoint.expected: Plane 1 lies on the top face and is selected (blue); the plane toolbar shows “Sketch on plane”.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".
steps.toolPath: Right-click a face › New plane here › On face

steps.title: Offset from face with live preview
steps.learn: Make a second plane 40 mm above the top face.
instructions: Right-click the top face › New plane here › Offset from face…
A ghost plane follows the value — type 40 (or drag the arrow) and press Enter.
Tip: you can also type a formula (40+5) or a parameter name.
steps.why: The preview shows exactly where the plane lands before you create it.

checkpoint.expected: Plane 2 floats 40 mm above the block. The orange dashed outline shows the face it comes from.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".
steps.toolPath: Right-click a face › New plane here › Offset from face…

steps.title: Drag the arrow to change the offset
steps.learn: A selected offset plane has a blue arrow with its distance.
instructions: Click the plane’s OUTLINE (or its name label) to select it — clicks on the transparent fill go through to the model.
Drag the blue arrow up to 60 mm, or click the “40 mm ⇕” tag and type 60.
steps.why: Planes never block clicks on the faces behind them: only the outline and the label select a plane.

checkpoint.expected: The plane is now 60 mm above the block.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".
steps.toolPath: Click the plane outline › drag the arrow

steps.title: Sketch on the plane
steps.learn: Press S (or double-click the plane) to start a sketch on it.
instructions: With the plane selected press S, or click ✏ Sketch on plane in the toolbar.
The outline of the parent face shows as dashed reference edges you can snap to.
Draw a circle Ø40 at the centre and click Finish.
steps.why: Offset planes show the face they come from, so you can line new geometry up with the existing part.

checkpoint.expected: A sketch with a Ø40 circle 60 mm above the block.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Extrude down to the block
steps.learn: Extrude the circle back down until it meets the top face.
instructions: Extrude the new sketch −60 mm (downwards) to join the block.
(Edit the extrude later: End › Up to Top plane makes it follow the plane automatically.)
steps.why: A post built from a raised plane — move the plane and the post grows with it.

checkpoint.expected: A Ø40 post standing on the block.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Extrude up to a plane
steps.learn: Use the plane toolbar ⋯ › Extrude a sketch up to it.
instructions: Sketch a 20 × 20 square at a corner of the top face.
Select Plane 40 up › ⋯ › Extrude a sketch up to it › choose the square.
The extrusion ends exactly on the plane and follows it if the plane moves.
steps.why: “Up to” ends are design intent: change the plane once, every feature that ends on it updates.

checkpoint.expected: A square pillar from the block up to the plane.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".
steps.toolPath: Plane toolbar › ⋯ › Extrude a sketch up to it

steps.title: A plane at an angle
steps.learn: Right-click a face › New plane here › At angle to face… then pick an edge to rotate about.
instructions: Here the plane is made from the YZ plane, turned 30° about the Z axis.
The panel previews the plane while you change the angle.
steps.why: Angle planes are how you make sloped cuts, ramps and chamfer-like walls.

checkpoint.expected: A vertical plane turned 30° through the middle of the block.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".
steps.toolPath: Right-click a face › New plane here › At angle to face…

steps.title: Mirror and split with planes
steps.learn: Planes drive other tools from the toolbar ⋯ menu.
instructions: Make a plane 70 mm from YZ (Reference ▾ › Plane… › Offset).
Select it › ⋯ › Mirror a body across it › Post.
Make a plane −30 mm from YZ › ⋯ › Split a body with it › Block.
steps.why: Mirror, split, section view and patterns all accept a reference plane and update with it.

checkpoint.expected: A mirrored post on the other side and the block split in two halves.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Pattern along a plane normal
steps.learn: Copy a body along the direction a plane faces.
instructions: Select Mirror plane › ⋯ › Pattern along its normal.
Count 3, spacing 25 mm (tick Other direction).
steps.why: The pattern direction comes from the plane — turn the plane and the pattern turns with it.

checkpoint.expected: Three pillars in a row along X.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".
steps.toolPath: Plane toolbar › ⋯ › Pattern along its normal

steps.title: Keyboard, colours and groups
steps.learn: Finish with the time savers.
instructions: S sketch on the selected plane · Esc deselect · Del delete · F2 rename · double-click a plane to sketch.
In Properties: set a colour and a group (e.g. “Datums”) — hide a whole group from the ▱ button beside the view cube (right-click it).
If a plane loses its face (you deleted it), a ⚠ warning offers “Re-pick base”.
steps.why: Colours and groups keep large models readable; Re-pick base repairs broken links in one click.

checkpoint.expected: Plane 40 up is green and in the group Datums.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Loft from a face to a single point (pyramid tip)
courses.objective: A loft section can now be one point. The last ring collapses to a vertex, so a square face becomes a pyramid.

steps.title: What a point section is
steps.learn: A normal loft joins two outlines. A point section is an outline of zero size: every ring point meets at one vertex. The solid closes by itself, no end cap is made at the tip.
instructions: Read this page. Nothing needs to be clicked yet.
A point can be: a corner of a solid, a point in a sketch, or typed X / Y / Z in the Loft dialog.
A point may only be the FIRST or the LAST section.
steps.why: Pyramids, cones, ogives and pointed nose shapes all start from a profile plus a point.
steps.toolPath: Model / DESIGN tab › Create ▾ › Loft      (AakarFORM tab › Loft & Sweep ▾ › Loft)

steps.title: Build the base block
steps.learn: The block is 40 x 40 x 10 mm. Its top face is the profile that will be lofted to the point.
instructions: Run this step to build the block and a helper circle.
For your own model, make any block or extrude.

checkpoint.expected: One block is visible.

steps.title: Loft the top face to a point
steps.learn: Open Model > Loft (or AakarFORM > Loft guides > Guided loft). Section 1 = the top face outer boundary, Section 2 = POINT typed X / Y / Z with Z = 45.
instructions: Run this step to build the example.
For your own model: open Loft, choose the top face as Section 1, choose 'POINT · typed X / Y / Z' as Section 2, then type X 0, Y 0, Z 45.
Use New body to inspect it first. Use Join if you want one body with the block.
steps.why: The volume of a pyramid is one third of base area times height. 40 x 40 x 35 / 3 = 18 666.7 mm3, and Aakar reports the same number.

checkpoint.expected: A pyramid sits on the block. Its volume is about 18 667 mm3.

steps.recovery: Nothing is broken. Press Ctrl+Z to undo, then press Build this step again. Aakar rebuilds exactly the values listed in the step.
steps.toolPath: Model / DESIGN tab › Create ▾ › Loft      (AakarFORM tab › Loft & Sweep ▾ › Loft)

steps.title: Troubleshooting
steps.learn: A point lying in the plane of the profile makes no volume. A point cannot be combined with sections that have holes.
instructions: If you see 'The point lies in the plane of the profile', change Z so the point is above or below the face.
If you see 'A point end cannot be combined with sections that have holes', remove the hole or end on a small circle instead.

courses.title: Loft from edges: a chain of edges to a point or a circle
courses.objective: Selected solid edges can be loft sections. Two or more connected edges are closed with a straight chord, so the loft is a solid.

steps.title: Why one edge is not enough
steps.learn: One straight edge has no inside. Two connected edges form an L; Aakar closes the L with a straight chord to get a triangle. A triangle plus a point is a solid with four faces.
instructions: Read this page.
You can pick edges in the model first (Shift-click for several) and then open Loft: they are offered as 'selected edges' in the section list.
Or, inside the Loft dialog, set 'List shows' to Solid edges, or click an edge in the 3D view.
steps.why: Edges let you build a transition straight from the geometry you already have.
steps.toolPath: Model / DESIGN tab › Create ▾ › Loft      (AakarFORM tab › Loft & Sweep ▾ › Loft)

steps.title: Build the base block
steps.learn: The top face has four edges. The demo picks two that meet at a corner.
instructions: Run this step to build the block.

steps.title: Two edges to a point
steps.learn: Section 1 = two connected top edges, Section 2 = a point above the block.
instructions: Run this step to build the example.
In your model: click the first edge in the 3D view, then Shift-click the next one, open Loft, and choose 'selected edges' as Section 1 and a point as Section 2.

checkpoint.expected: A tetrahedron-like solid sits on the corner of the block. The result carries a note that the open edge chain was closed with a chord.

steps.recovery: Nothing is broken. Press Ctrl+Z to undo, then press Build this step again. Aakar rebuilds exactly the values listed in the step.
steps.toolPath: Model / DESIGN tab › Create ▾ › Loft      (AakarFORM tab › Loft & Sweep ▾ › Loft)

steps.title: Two edges to a circle
steps.learn: The same chain can end on a circle. The circle is a full outline, the chain is closed with a chord.
instructions: Run this step to build the second example.
In your model choose the circle sketch as Section 2.

checkpoint.expected: A transition solid joins the corner chain to the circle.

courses.title: Loft a face with a hole to a ring
courses.objective: Sections may now have holes. The outer outlines are lofted together and the hole outlines are lofted together, giving a hollow transition.

steps.title: Matching holes
steps.learn: Both sections must have the same number of holes. Aakar pairs each hole with the nearest hole of the next section and lofts them as an inner tube.
instructions: Read this page.
In the section list, choose the entry that says 'outer boundary + 1 hole(s)' for a face with a hole.
A sketch with two nested circles is already one profile with one hole.
steps.why: Pipes, funnels and hollow adapters are lofts of a ring to a ring.

steps.title: Build the block with a hole and the ring sketch
steps.learn: The block has a 10 mm hole. The ring sketch at Z = 40 has an outer circle R12 and an inner circle R6.
instructions: Run this step to build both.

steps.title: Loft ring to face-with-hole
steps.learn: Section 1 = top face outer boundary + hole, Section 2 = the ring sketch.
instructions: Run this step to build the example.
In your model: open Loft, choose 'outer boundary + 1 hole(s)' for Section 1 and the ring sketch for Section 2.

checkpoint.expected: A hollow solid rises from the block; its hole follows through the ring.

steps.recovery: Nothing is broken. Press Ctrl+Z to undo, then press Build this step again. Aakar rebuilds exactly the values listed in the step.
steps.toolPath: Model / DESIGN tab › Create ▾ › Loft      (AakarFORM tab › Loft & Sweep ▾ › Loft)

steps.title: Mismatched holes
steps.learn: If one section has a hole and the other does not, Aakar stops and says so instead of guessing.
instructions: Try choosing a plain circle as Section 2: the message 'All sections need the same number of holes' appears.
Fix it by choosing a ring with a hole, or by choosing only the outer boundary of the face.

courses.title: Control the shape: tangent ends, twist, reverse and start offset
courses.objective: Tangent strength makes the loft leave the profile straight (perpendicular to it), twist winds the transition, and reverse / start offset change which points connect.

steps.title: The four controls
steps.learn: Tangent ends: strength 0 is off, 1 leaves the profile straight out. Twist: rotates the transition, both end profiles stay exact. Reverse and Start offset: change which point of one outline joins which point of the other.
instructions: Read this page.
In the Loft dialog tick 'Shape' for tangent and twist, and 'Alignment' for reverse and start offset.
steps.toolPath: Model / DESIGN tab › Create ▾ › Loft      (AakarFORM tab › Loft & Sweep ▾ › Loft)

steps.title: Straight loft for comparison
steps.learn: This is the ordinary loft from the block top to the circle.
instructions: Run this step to build it.

steps.title: Tangent at both ends
steps.learn: Strength 1 at the start and the end. The sides of the transition continue the side walls of the block and arrive at the circle straight.
instructions: Run this step to build the tangent version.
In your model set Start tangent strength 1 and End tangent strength 1, then compare the shape.

checkpoint.expected: The tangent loft bulges more than the straight one and leaves the block face squarely.

steps.recovery: Nothing is broken. Press Ctrl+Z to undo, then press Build this step again. Aakar rebuilds exactly the values listed in the step.

steps.title: Twist
steps.learn: A square is lofted to a smaller square with a 60 degree twist. Each corner of the top joins a corner that is wound around the axis.
instructions: Run this step to build the twisted tower.
In your model set Twist per gap to 60.

checkpoint.expected: The faces of the transition spiral.

steps.recovery: Nothing is broken. Press Ctrl+Z to undo, then press Build this step again. Aakar rebuilds exactly the values listed in the step.

steps.title: Start offset
steps.learn: The start offset moves where the outline begins, in percent around the outline. 25 percent turns the connection a quarter turn.
instructions: Run this step to build the example.
In your model tick Alignment, then change Start offset of section 2 to 25.

checkpoint.expected: The transition is visibly turned compared with the straight loft.

steps.recovery: Nothing is broken. Press Ctrl+Z to undo, then press Build this step again. Aakar rebuilds exactly the values listed in the step.

courses.title: Pick sections on screen: names, colours and the curve list
courses.objective: The Loft dialog now shows every curve with a colour and a name in the 3D view, lets you click curves instead of using drop-downs, and has a curve list with eye icons.

steps.title: The colours
steps.learn: Section 1 is orange and says START, Section 2 is blue, Section 3 purple, Section 4 yellow, Section 5 pink, Section 6 green. Guide rails are mint green. Hovering a curve in the 3D view turns it white and shows its name.
instructions: Read this page.
The checkbox 'Show curve names in the 3D view' turns the name tags on and off. Your choice is remembered.

steps.title: Build the block and the circle
steps.learn: You need something to pick.
instructions: Run this step to build the block and the circle.

steps.title: Pick by clicking
steps.learn: Open Loft. Click the circle in the 3D view and the active section (shown in the curve list title) is filled. Click a block edge and it fills the next section.
instructions: Open Model > Loft.
Click curves in the 3D view. If several curves lie on top of each other (a cube edge is also the border of two faces), click again at the same spot to cycle through them. The hover tag says '1 of 3'.
Use 'List shows' to limit the drop-downs to sketches, faces, edges, points or curves.

checkpoint.expected: The name tags S1 and S2 appear next to the chosen curves.

steps.toolPath: Model / DESIGN tab › Create ▾ › Loft      (AakarFORM tab › Loft & Sweep ▾ › Loft)

steps.title: The curve list and eye icons
steps.learn: The list on the left names every curve. The eye shows or hides a curve in the 3D view, 'Show all' and 'Hide all' do it for the whole list. Clicking a name uses it for the active section.
instructions: Press Show all to see every candidate curve.
Hover a name to see the curve in white in the 3D view.
Press the small 'fold' button to hide the list if it is in the way.

courses.title: Sweep along a path made of a cube edge and a 3D curve
courses.objective: The sweep path can now be a sketch, a 3D curve, a face boundary or solid edges, and up to four pieces are joined end to end.

steps.title: Profile and path
steps.learn: A sweep drags a profile (a sketch) along a path. Before 8.70 the path had to be a sketch. Now each path piece can be a sketch, a 3D sketch curve, the boundary of a face, or solid edges. Several pieces are joined end to end.
instructions: Read this page.
In Model > Sweep you now see 'Path piece 1' to 'Path piece 4' instead of one path sketch.
Click a curve in the 3D view to fill the active path piece. Colours: orange = profile, blue / purple = path pieces.
steps.why: Pipes, rails and handles often start on a cube edge and then curve away. Now that route is one sweep.
steps.toolPath: Model / DESIGN tab › Create ▾ › Sweep      (AakarFORM tab › Loft & Sweep ▾ › Sweep)

steps.title: Build the block and the 3D curve
steps.learn: The block is 40 x 40 x 10 mm. The 3D curve starts at the top corner (20, -20, 10) and rises to (20, 20, 40).
instructions: Run this step to build both.

steps.title: Add the round profile
steps.learn: A circle of radius 3 mm sits at the other end of the top edge, on a plane that crosses the edge.
instructions: Run this step to add the profile sketch.
For your own model: draw the profile on a plane that is not parallel to the start of the path.

steps.title: Sweep along edge then curve
steps.learn: Path piece 1 = the top edge, Path piece 2 = the 3D curve. They meet at the corner (20, -20, 10). Aakar decides the direction by itself so the pieces meet end to end.
instructions: Run this step to build the tube.
For your own model: open Model > Sweep, choose the profile sketch, then choose the edge as Path piece 1 and the curve as Path piece 2. Or click them in the 3D view.

checkpoint.expected: A round tube runs along the top edge, then follows the rising curve.

steps.recovery: Nothing is broken. Press Ctrl+Z to undo, then press Build this step again.
steps.toolPath: Model / DESIGN tab › Create ▾ › Sweep      (AakarFORM tab › Loft & Sweep ▾ › Sweep)

steps.title: When pieces do not meet
steps.learn: If two pieces do not touch, Aakar says which piece and how big the gap is, instead of guessing.
instructions: Try choosing a piece that starts somewhere else: the message 'Path piece 2 does not touch piece 1 (gap ...)' appears.
Fix it by moving the curve end onto the edge end, or add a short connecting piece. 'Reverse the path direction' flips the whole path.

courses.title: Twist a sweep and keep the profile orientation
courses.objective: Twist rotates the profile steadily along the path. 'Keep the profile orientation' stops the profile from turning with the path.

steps.title: Two controls
steps.learn: Twist is the total rotation in degrees from the start to the end of the path. The profile orientation option decides if the profile turns with the path (Follow) or keeps its original direction (Keep, only for gentle paths).
instructions: Read this page.

steps.title: Build the path and a square profile

instructions: Run this step to build the example.

instructions: Run this step to build the twisted bar.

steps.learn: Set 'Profile orientation' to 'Keep the profile orientation'. If the path turns too far, Aakar stops with a message and asks you to use Follow or to split the path.

courses.title: Make a rail: line, arc or spline from a cube edge to a circle
courses.objective: A rail is a guide curve for Loft. It starts on a face, edge or corner of the cube and ends on another curve. It stays attached to both, so it follows the cube when the cube changes.

steps.title: Where the tools are
steps.learn: Everything lives in one place now. Loft and Loft rail are in the Create menu: Model / DESIGN tab, then Create, then Loft or Loft rail. In the AakarFORM tab they are in the group called Loft & Sweep. The old 'Loft guides' group is gone.
instructions: Click the Model (DESIGN) tab.
Open the Create menu. You will see Extrude, Revolve, Sweep, Loft and Loft rail.
Press 'Show me the tool' below and the Loft rail button will blink.

steps.title: Build the block and the circle

instructions: Run this step to build both.

courses.title: Four rails and three sections
courses.objective: Loft takes any number of rails and any number of sections. A rail through a middle section pulls that section into the shape.

steps.title: The rule for rails
steps.learn: Rails run from the first section to the last section. Between them they may pass through the middle sections. At least one rail is needed; more rails give tighter control. Two rails must not cross.
instructions: Read this page.

instructions: Run this step to build the example.

steps.learn: Start tangent 1 and end tangent 1 make the loft leave the block straight up and arrive at the circle straight, while the rail still holds the shape in between.

courses.title: Reference images · import, re-orient, see-through, zoom and draw a bottle
courses.objective: Import a picture, put it on a plane, rotate / mirror / tilt it, make it see-through, zoom it to true size, move it with the mouse, then draw over it and revolve a solid bottle.

steps.title: What a reference image is (read this first)
steps.learn: A REFERENCE IMAGE is a picture you place inside the 3D view, like tracing paper: a photo, a sketch or a drawing of the thing you want to make. It is NOT part of the model; it only helps you draw the right shape and size.
instructions: Read this page. Nothing needs to be clicked yet.
Designers use reference images all the time: a side photo of a bottle, a drawing of a bracket, a car blueprint.
In Aakar you can: import a picture, put it on any plane (Top, Front, Right …), turn and mirror it, make it see-through, zoom it bigger or smaller, and then draw your sketch over it.
Where to find it: Model tab → group “Ref images” → Ref image (the panel) or Import pic (opens a file at once).
Shortcuts: drop a picture file onto the 3D view, or copy a picture and press Ctrl+V in the 3D view.
Press Next step ▶ when ready.
steps.why: Drawing over a real picture is the fastest way to get believable proportions, even if you cannot draw well by hand.

checkpoint.expected: You know where the Ref images group is, and that a reference image is only a guide.

steps.recovery: Nothing is broken. Press Ctrl+Z (hold the Ctrl key and tap Z) to undo, then press ▶ Build this step again. Aakar always builds exactly the values listed under “Aakar will build”.

steps.title: Bring in a picture (the sample bottle)
steps.learn: IMPORT = bring a file into Aakar. The picture is placed on a PLANE: a flat, endless sheet in 3D. FRONT plane = the sheet you look at from the front (X to the right, Z up).
instructions: Model tab → Ref images → Ref image. The “Reference images” panel opens on the right.
Click Sample. A side view of a bottle, 120 × 200 mm, appears standing on the Front plane.
With your own pictures you would click “+ Import…” (or drop the file on the 3D view, or press Ctrl+V).
“New pictures go on” chooses the plane for the next import: “Plane facing the view” picks Top, Front or Right, whichever faces you most.
Or press ▶ Build this step.
steps.why: A picture on a real plane stays put when you turn the view, so you can check your model against it from any angle.

checkpoint.expected: The bottle picture stands upright on the ground grid, seen from the front. “Sample · bottle” is listed in the panel.

steps.recovery: Nothing is broken. Press Ctrl+Z (hold the Ctrl key and tap Z) to undo, then press ▶ Build this step again. Aakar always builds exactly the values listed under “Aakar will build”.

steps.title: Make it see-through and grey
steps.learn: OPACITY (see-through) = how solid the picture looks. 100% hides what is behind it, 30% lets you see your sketch lines and the model clearly through it.
instructions: In the panel, section Look: drag “See-through” down to about 35%.
Tick Grey: the colours go away, so your orange and blue sketch lines stand out.
Untick “Always in front of the model” for now: the model then hides the parts of the picture behind it, like in real life.
Or press ▶ Build this step.
steps.why: A faint, grey picture is easy to trace over; a bright, coloured one fights with your lines.

checkpoint.expected: The bottle picture is pale grey and you can see the grid through it.

steps.recovery: Nothing is broken. Press Ctrl+Z (hold the Ctrl key and tap Z) to undo, then press ▶ Build this step again. Aakar always builds exactly the values listed under “Aakar will build”.

steps.title: Re-orient: rotate, mirror, tilt
steps.learn: RE-ORIENT = turn the picture so it lines up with your model. ROTATE turns it flat on its plane. MIRROR swaps left and right. TILT leans it forward/back (↕) or sideways (↔) off the plane.
instructions: Section Re-orient: click ⟳90 once. The bottle lies on its side.
Click ↔ Mirror. The picture is flipped left-to-right.
Try the Tilt ↕ slider: the picture leans like an easel. Put it back to 0.
Plane buttons (Top, Front, Right, Back, Left, Bottom, View) move the picture onto another plane in one click. View = facing the camera exactly as it is now.
Or press ▶ Build this step (rotate 90° + mirror).
steps.why: Photos are rarely straight. Rotating by a few degrees until a known edge is horizontal is the first thing to do with any real picture.

checkpoint.expected: The bottle lies on its side and is mirrored.

steps.recovery: Nothing is broken. Press Ctrl+Z (hold the Ctrl key and tap Z) to undo, then press ▶ Build this step again. Aakar always builds exactly the values listed under “Aakar will build”.

steps.title: Straighten it again (Reset)
steps.learn: RESET puts rotation, tilt and mirror back to zero, but keeps the size, position and see-through.
instructions: Click Reset in the Flip row.
The bottle stands upright again, not mirrored.
Or press ▶ Build this step.
steps.why: You can always experiment: one click brings the picture back to straight.

checkpoint.expected: The bottle stands upright, the right way round.

steps.recovery: Nothing is broken. Press Ctrl+Z (hold the Ctrl key and tap Z) to undo, then press ▶ Build this step again. Aakar always builds exactly the values listed under “Aakar will build”.

steps.title: Zoom the picture in and out, then give it its true size
steps.learn: ZOOM changes the SIZE of the picture (not the camera). TRUE SIZE means 1 mm on the picture = 1 mm in Aakar, so what you trace has the right dimensions. CALIBRATE = tell Aakar the real distance between two points you can see on the picture.
instructions: Section Size & zoom: click 2×. The picture doubles. Click ½× to go back.
− Out / + In change the size by 10% each click.
True size, way 1: type the real width in Width (the height follows, the shape never stretches). The sample is 120 mm wide.
True size, way 2: click ↔ Calibrate from 2 points, click the left and right ends of the Ø72 line on the bottle, type 72 in “real” and click Apply.
Position: X · Y · Z is the centre of the picture. “Stand on Z = 0” puts its lower edge on the ground.
Or press ▶ Build this step (width 120 mm, centre 0, 0, 93).
steps.why: Tracing a picture that is the wrong size gives a model of the wrong size. Calibrating once against a known dimension fixes it.

checkpoint.expected: The picture is 120 × 200 mm. The bottom of the bottle sits on the red X axis (Z = 0) and the centre line is on the blue Z axis.

steps.recovery: Nothing is broken. Press Ctrl+Z (hold the Ctrl key and tap Z) to undo, then press ▶ Build this step again. Aakar always builds exactly the values listed under “Aakar will build”.

steps.title: Move it with the mouse (Adjust in view)
steps.learn: ADJUST IN VIEW lets you grab the picture in the 3D view itself. Dragging empty space still turns the view as usual.
instructions: Click ✜ Adjust in view. An orange frame with handles appears around the picture.
Drag the picture = move it on its plane.
Shift + drag = rotate it around its centre (hold Alt as well to snap in 15° steps).
Ctrl + drag = make it bigger or smaller.
Mouse wheel over the picture = zoom the picture around the mouse. Shift + wheel = more or less see-through.
Press Esc (or click ✓ Done adjusting) when finished. Ctrl+Z undoes any move.
Press ▶ Build this step to switch the mode on, play, then press Ctrl+Z if you moved it and press Esc.
steps.why: Lining a picture up by hand is quicker than typing numbers when you only need it roughly in place.

checkpoint.expected: The orange frame shows around the picture and dragging it moves it.

steps.recovery: Nothing is broken. Press Ctrl+Z (hold the Ctrl key and tap Z) to undo, then press ▶ Build this step again. Aakar always builds exactly the values listed under “Aakar will build”.

steps.title: Draw on the picture: trace the half profile
steps.learn: DRAW ON THIS PICTURE opens a SKETCH on exactly the picture’s plane, with the picture showing underneath. A round bottle only needs HALF of its outline (the PROFILE): Revolve spins it round the centre line.
instructions: Press Esc to leave Adjust mode if it is still on.
Click ✎ Draw on this picture. The 2D sketch opens with the bottle under the grid.

Choose the Line tool and click along the RIGHT half of the bottle: start on the dashed red centre line at the bottom, go right along the base, up the side, in at the shoulder, up the neck, along the top, and back down the centre line to the start.
Click Finish. “Bottle profile (traced)” appears in the feature list.
Or press ▶ Build this step: Aakar draws the same outline for you.
steps.why: Tracing only the half you need keeps the sketch small and lets Revolve guarantee a perfectly round bottle.

checkpoint.expected: A closed outline of the right half of the bottle lies exactly on the picture.

steps.recovery: Nothing is broken. Press Ctrl+Z (hold the Ctrl key and tap Z) to undo, then press ▶ Build this step again. Aakar always builds exactly the values listed under “Aakar will build”.
steps.toolPath: Ref images panel › ✎ Draw on this picture

steps.title: Revolve it into a solid bottle
steps.learn: REVOLVE spins a profile 360° around an axis, like a potter’s wheel.
instructions: Model tab → Create → Revolve.
Sketch: “Bottle profile (traced)”. Axis: the sketch’s vertical (Y) axis, the centre line. Angle: 360.
Click OK. A solid bottle appears, the same size as the picture.
Or press ▶ Build this step.
steps.why: Picture → trace → revolve is the classic way to model bottles, vases, knobs and turned parts from a photo.

checkpoint.expected: One solid bottle, 72 mm across and 186 mm tall.

steps.recovery: Nothing is broken. Press Ctrl+Z (hold the Ctrl key and tap Z) to undo, then press ▶ Build this step again. Aakar always builds exactly the values listed under “Aakar will build”.

steps.title: Check the model against the picture
steps.learn: ALWAYS IN FRONT draws the picture over the model, so you can compare edges. Hide (eye icon) turns the picture off without deleting it.
instructions: In the panel tick “Always in front of the model” and set See-through to 50%.
Click the Front view button: the outline of the solid should sit exactly on the drawing.
Click ◎ Look at it to aim the camera straight at any picture.
Click the eye icon to hide the picture, again to show it. The trash (✕) deletes it.
Save the project: reference images are saved with it.
Or press ▶ Build this step.
steps.why: Checking against the reference at the end catches tracing mistakes before you add details.

checkpoint.expected: From the front, the bottle and the picture match line for line.

steps.recovery: Nothing is broken. Press Ctrl+Z (hold the Ctrl key and tap Z) to undo, then press ▶ Build this step again. Aakar always builds exactly the values listed under “Aakar will build”.

courses.title: Bathroom Washbasin
courses.objective: Loft a basin bowl down to its drain, build a flat counter deck, join them with a G2 blend, trim a tap hole, check the highlights and thicken it into ceramic.

steps.title: Bowl sections
steps.learn: Five sections from the 220 × 150 rim down to the Ø40 drain.
instructions: NURBS › Sketch on XY at Z 0, −30, −75, −102 and −112.
Rounded ovals: 220×150, 200×132, 150×96, 80×54, then a Ø40 circle.
steps.why: The spacing of the sections sets the bowl shape: steep sides, a soft floor and a round drain.

checkpoint.expected: Five stacked closed curves getting smaller downward.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".
steps.say: A bowl is not drawn in one go. We draw five flat outlines, each on its own invisible sheet of paper (a plane) at a different height, like slices of a cake. Each sheet starts at the floor and is slid up or down by typing a number called the Offset (0, -30, -75, -102, -112 mm). Nothing is dragged in 3D. The next step joins the five outlines into one smooth bowl.

steps.title: Loft the bowl
steps.learn: Loft rim to drain, degree 3.
instructions: NURBS › Loft: the five sections from top to bottom.
steps.why: The last section is the drain, so the outlet is already the correct size.

checkpoint.expected: A deep bowl open at the drain.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Counter deck
steps.learn: The deck is a flat ring: an inner oval 250 × 180 and an outer 440 × 300 rectangle, both at Z 15.
instructions: NURBS › Sketch on XY at Z 15: inner oval 250 × 180.
A second sketch at Z 15: outer rounded rectangle 440 × 300.
NURBS › Loft the two curves.
steps.why: Lofting two curves in the same plane gives a flat surface with a hole: an ideal deck.

checkpoint.expected: A flat deck with an oval opening above the bowl.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: G2 blend bowl to deck
steps.learn: The rim of the bowl is 15 mm below the deck. Fill the gap with a curvature-continuous blend.
instructions: NURBS+ › Blend: A = bowl, edge v0 (rim), G2; B = deck, edge v0 (opening), G2; bulge 1.
steps.why: G2 means the curvature flows across the joint, so no hard line appears where the bowl meets the deck.

checkpoint.expected: A soft rolled edge between deck and bowl.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Tap hole outline
steps.learn: A Ø35 tap hole sits on the centre line, 120 mm behind the bowl centre.
instructions: NURBS › Sketch on XY: circle Ø35 at (0, 120).
steps.why: Sketch flat, then project it. The deck is flat, so the hole stays round.

checkpoint.expected: A circle on the deck behind the bowl.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Trim the tap hole
steps.learn: Project the circle along Z and remove what is inside.
instructions: NURBS+ › Trim: deck, tap-hole sketch, +Z, keep outside.
steps.why: Trimming hides the inside region; the deck surface itself is untouched.

checkpoint.expected: A round hole in the deck.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Zebra check
steps.learn: Look at the stripes around the rim.
instructions: NURBS+ › Zebra.
steps.why: Stripes that run smoothly across the blend confirm G2. A kink would show as a reflection break on glazed ceramic.

checkpoint.expected: Continuous stripes from deck to bowl.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Thicken into ceramic
steps.learn: Ceramic basins have a 6 mm wall. Thicken the three surfaces.
instructions: Turn Zebra and Comb off first (NURBS+ › Zebra / Comb).
NURBS › Thicken: bowl 6 mm, blend 6 mm, deck 6 mm.
steps.why: Each skin becomes a solid with the same wall, ready to section and check.

checkpoint.expected: A solid basin with deck and tap hole.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Round-to-Rectangle Air Duct
courses.objective: Loft an HVAC transition from a 120 × 80 rectangular port to a Ø70 round outlet, add a 90° bend, extend a straight flange, then offset a liner and thicken everything into sheet metal.

steps.title: Three port sections
steps.learn: A transition duct is defined by its two ports plus one in-between shape that controls how fast the corners round off.
instructions: NURBS › Sketch on XY at Z 0: a rounded rectangle 120 × 80 (squarish, closed spline).
At Z 35: a softer shape 100 × 76.
At Z 80: a circle Ø70.
All three curves use 16 points that start on the +X side.
steps.why: Lofts follow the point order. Starting every section at the same place stops the duct twisting.

checkpoint.expected: Three closed curves stacked up the Z axis.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Loft the transition
steps.learn: Loft through the three sections, degree 3.
instructions: NURBS › Loft: pick rectangle, transition and circle in that order, degree 3.
steps.why: The middle section makes the change from square to round gradual, so the air flows smoothly.

checkpoint.expected: A smooth square-to-round duct.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Rebuild a clean net
steps.learn: Rebuild to an even 14 × 8 control net.
instructions: NURBS › Rebuild: 14 × 8, degree 3 × 3.
steps.why: An even net offsets and thickens more reliably.

checkpoint.expected: Same shape, tidier control points.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Bend path
steps.learn: The bend follows a quarter circle of radius 90 from the top of the duct.
instructions: NURBS › Sketch on XZ: a spline through seven points of a quarter circle, centre (90, 80), radius 90.
steps.why: A pipe or sweep needs a path. Starting the path at the outlet centre keeps the bend attached.

checkpoint.expected: A quarter arc rising from the outlet.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Sweep the 90° bend
steps.learn: Pipe a Ø70 circle along the path.
instructions: NURBS › Pipe: path = bend path, radius 35 at both ends, 36 stations.
steps.why: A pipe is a sweep of a circle, so the bend matches the round outlet exactly.

checkpoint.expected: A 90° elbow on top of the transition.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Extend a flange
steps.learn: Extend the rectangular end straight down by 15 mm as its own surface.
instructions: NURBS+ › Extend: duct, edge v0 (first section), 15 mm, linear, merge off.
steps.why: Linear extension continues the tangent, giving a straight collar for the clamp. Keeping it separate lets you thicken or change it on its own.

checkpoint.expected: A straight 15 mm collar below the rectangular port.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Check the transition
steps.learn: Curvature combs show how evenly the corners open up.
instructions: NURBS+ › Comb, then NURBS+ › Zebra.
steps.why: Kinks in the stripes mean noise and pressure loss in a real duct.

checkpoint.expected: Smooth combs and continuous stripes.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Offset a liner
steps.learn: Offset the duct 3 mm inward as a copy, for an insulation liner.
instructions: NURBS+ › Offset+: duct, −3 mm, copy.
steps.why: An offset is exact at every point, so the gap is constant.

checkpoint.expected: A second skin inside the duct.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Thicken into sheet metal

instructions: Turn Zebra and Comb off first (NURBS+ › Zebra / Comb).
NURBS › Thicken: duct, flange and bend, 1.5 mm each.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.objective: See what degree, knots and control points do to the same surface: raise the degree, insert and remove knots, then rebuild.

steps.title: Three section curves
steps.learn: A surface is lofted through three curves at different positions.
instructions: NURBS › Sketch on XZ planes at Y −35, 0 and 35.
Each is a fit-point spline with five points.
steps.why: The curves are the data; the degree and knot vector are how the maths interprets them.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Loft at degree 2

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Raise the degree
